title: Turbo and CI Cache Efficiency Implementation Tasks
principles: Treat Turbo, Bun packages and Playwright Chromium as separate cache layers.
Route every eligible deterministic root and workspace command through Turbo tasks.
Keep the full uncached release graph as the correctness path.
Apply Vercel Remote Cache to pull requests, main, trusted deployment/receipt workflows and explicit local opt-in with event-scoped write safety.
Measure cache hits, misses, fallback and accepted outcome rather than activity.

globalVerification.commitPolicy: Implementation commits are allowed only after the task-local gates, owner documentation updates, cache authority decision and parent review pass. This SPEC itself is planning-only.
evidenceRequired: Current cold baseline and one warm observation for each cache layer.
Pull-request and main Vercel Remote Cache hits plus forced uncached Turbo proof.
A remote-cache hit from at least one trusted deployment or receipt workflow while its provider and receipt boundaries remain live.
Bun package-cache and Playwright Chromium-cache hit/miss observations.
Exact source revision, workflow run, cache-key digest, postcondition, rollback and non-claims for each hosted observation.
Evidence that pull-request code cannot overwrite trusted cache entries and that its read-safe or isolated-write credential boundary is enforced.
Updated policy, controls, architecture, runbook and lifecycle-owner records.

downstreamArtifactImpact.verification: bun run check:quality-workflow and bun run test:quality-workflow
nonClaims: A green local policy check does not prove a hosted cache hit or Vercel provider state.

downstreamArtifactImpact.verification: bunx turbo run build --force, bunx turbo run check-types --force, and bun run release:check -- --ci
nonClaims: The release orchestrator does not become the owner of Turbo cache policy.

downstreamArtifactImpact.verification: Hosted cold/warm observations plus the existing install and browser proof commands
nonClaims: A cached Chromium binary does not prove runner system dependencies or hosted browser behaviour.

downstreamArtifactImpact.verification: bun run check:docs-deployment, bun run check:docs-deployment-automation, bun run test:docs-deployment, and authorised hosted workflow readback
nonClaims: Cache setup does not establish Preview, Production, rollback, public availability or provider state.

downstreamArtifactImpact.surface: Durable CI documentation and operational recovery
downstreamArtifactImpact.verification: bun run check:docs, bun run check:runbooks and bun run verification
nonClaims: Dated cache observations are not current provider policy or public deployment proof.

downstreamArtifactImpact.surface: Packages, public APIs, app runtime and Changesets
downstreamArtifactImpact.verification: Explicit no-Changeset rationale; package and runtime owners remain unchanged.
nonClaims: No package version, export, API, SDK, public docs or app runtime change is implied.

downstreamArtifactImpact.verification: Use the existing release-closure journey and retain dated cache receipts outside the profile.
nonClaims: Cache proof does not create a new consumer-visible journey or general harness-effectiveness claim.

tasks.title: Qualify cache inputs, authority and cold baseline
tasks.goal: Establish the smallest safe cache contract before changing workflow execution.
scope: Vercel Remote Cache team setting and GitHub/local credential boundaries, as separately authorised external resources
outputs: Cold baseline for Quality install, browser setup and release checks.
Turbo task input/output and environment audit.
Cache key design for Turbo, Bun packages and Playwright Chromium.
Run-specific authority envelope naming principal, team, token scope, expiry, revocation, rollback and readback.
Explicit event matrix covering local opt-in, pull-request read-safe or isolated write, main read/write, and trusted deployment/receipt read/write.
tasks.implementationPrompt: Review the current and target call graphs in the SPEC. Do not attach credentials or change workflows until the authority envelope is complete. Audit every command in Quality, deployment and receipt workflows and the nine-check release graph. Use Turbo root tasks for deterministic root commands and existing package tasks for workspace commands, but classify installs, external inputs, provider mutations/readback and stateful receipt work as live when their inputs cannot be safely hashed. Audit turbo.json for environment-sensitive tasks and incomplete inputs. Confirm that Bun's package cache and Playwright's browser cache are distinct. Record worker duration, feedback latency, synchronous maintainer attention and time to accepted outcome for the existing cold path.
browserVerification: Record the existing Playwright Chromium install and browser identity without treating the observation as hosted deployment proof.
qualityAudits: Review Turbo task inputs, outputs, global dependencies and environment sensitivity against the actual scripts and package manifests.
Review the cache trust boundary for pull-request credential exposure, namespace poisoning, task-log leakage and provider readback.
Review the baseline against the current one-job Quality graph and preserve the full nine-check path.
Review the authority envelope for exact principal, resource, environment, expiry, revocation, rollback and escalation.

parentAudit.basis: Review the baseline evidence, cache key design, target call graph, authority envelope and path-evidenced impact ledger.
parentAudit.recovery: Stop before workflow changes when cache inputs, token scope, PR trust or rollback cannot be resolved; correct, re-scope or seek a decision.

completionCriteria: The cold baseline is addressable and distinguishes worker time from queue or feedback time.
Turbo cache correctness inputs are either confirmed or named as an explicit blocker.
The external Vercel/GitHub authority envelope is accepted by the named owner or the task is recorded as blocked with a resume trigger.
The target event matrix is explicit: local opt-in, pull-request read-safe or isolated write, main/deployment/receipt read-write, and cache-miss fallback.
The parent agent accepted the task before workflow mutation begins.

tasks.title: Route Quality commands through Turbo and enable Vercel Remote Cache
tasks.goal: Reuse correct Turbo task artifacts for every eligible pull-request and main Quality command without weakening event safety or the full release graph.
scope: affected workspace package.json files if a task entrypoint changes
outputs: TURBO_TOKEN and TURBO_TEAM binding for every eligible Quality invocation under the approved pull-request/main event policy.
Turbo root-task mapping for cacheable root validators and report-only release commands without self-recursive scripts.
Full-SHA action and workflow policy coverage for any changed cache steps.
Remote-cache hit and forced uncached receipts for the same source candidate.
Pull-request coverage proving the approved read-safe or isolated-write boundary cannot overwrite trusted main cache entries.
tasks.implementationPrompt: Keep pull_request and push: main triggers, read-only repository permissions, timeout, concurrency and complete history. Preserve the report-only release-readiness semantics and exact nine-check graph; if the workflow command becomes a Turbo root-task wrapper, update the Quality policy, controls and README owners atomically rather than admitting a second graph. Route every eligible deterministic Quality command through Turbo; preserve @taxkit/scripts as the release orchestrator and keep candidate-mode/stateful commands live. Bind the approved cache-only credential or read-safe/isolated PR credential according to the event matrix; do not silently remove PR remote caching. Do not add pull_request_target, a second job, path filters, affected selection or cache-only success. Keep cache-service failure on the complete uncached path. Update policy, controls and durable owners in the same slice.
browserVerification: Run a hosted Quality candidate with the complete docs browser check and retain the exact run, cache-hit observation and browser postcondition.
Run the same candidate with Turbo cache bypass and confirm the complete graph still passes.
qualityAudits: Review remote-cache task inputs, outputs, environment variables and log contents.
Review that pull-request execution receives only the approved cache authority and cannot write the trusted main namespace.
Review that every deterministic root command is represented by a Turbo root task or an owning workspace task, with no self-recursive wrapper.
Review that remote cache is acceleration only and cannot change release command order, true exit status or proof ownership.
Review full-SHA action pins, permissions, timeout and concurrency against the existing Quality policy.

parentAudit.basis: Review the workflow and policy diff, remote-cache receipt, forced uncached result, hosted Quality run and documentation impact ledger.
parentAudit.recovery: Remove the cache environment and revert the workflow/policy change while retaining the complete uncached Quality graph if a hit, fallback, secret or proof condition is unsafe.

completionCriteria: A pull-request run and a trusted main run each record a remote Turbo cache hit for an eligible task.
A forced uncached run of the same candidate passes the same release graph.
A pull-request fixture or hosted inspection proves the approved credential/namespace boundary and no trusted main cache write occurs.
Every eligible Quality command is routed through Turbo while installs and stateful proof boundaries remain live.
Cache outage or missing token leaves the complete graph runnable and does not produce a false success.
Durable controls, architecture and runbook pointers are updated before acceptance.
No provider deployment, publication or public-availability claim is made.

tasks.title: Add Bun package and Playwright Chromium caches to every Quality event
tasks.goal: Avoid repeated package and browser downloads while retaining frozen installation and browser proof.
scope: bun.lock and .bun-version for cache identity only
outputs: Full-SHA restore/save actions for the Bun global package cache.
Full-SHA restore/save actions for the Playwright Chromium cache.
Explicit cache directories outside the checkout.
Lockfile, Bun-version, operating-system and Playwright-version cache keys.
Event-scoped restore/save behaviour for pull requests and main without cross-event cache poisoning.
tasks.implementationPrompt: Use Bun's resolved package-cache directory rather than caching node_modules. Keep bun install --frozen-lockfile. Set an explicit Playwright browser directory outside the checkout and cache Chromium separately from Bun packages. Preserve the existing --with-deps Quality policy in this task; do not claim that a browser cache covers operating-system packages. Restore and save on every configured Quality event only within the event-appropriate cache scope; pull-request entries must not overwrite trusted main entries. Save only after successful installation and keep cache failure non-fatal.
browserVerification: Observe one cold Chromium cache and one warm Chromium cache.
Run the complete docs browser test after the warm restore.
Record browser identity and distinguish binary restore from system-dependency installation.
qualityAudits: Review cache paths for checkout contamination, platform-specific files and stale node_modules reuse.
Review key invalidation for Bun version, lockfile, operating system and resolved Playwright version.
Review action pins and event-scoped save conditions for pull-request cache poisoning.
Review that install and browser commands remain visible and complete after a cache hit.

parentAudit.basis: Review the workflow/policy diff, cold/warm cache observations, browser proof, exact keys and documentation impact ledger.
parentAudit.recovery: Disable restore/save steps and retain frozen install/browser setup if a cache hit is stale, incomplete, poisoned or not measurably useful.

completionCriteria: A warm run reuses Bun package data without skipping frozen installation.
A warm run reuses the Playwright Chromium binary and still completes browser proof.
A lockfile, Bun version, OS or Playwright version change invalidates the corresponding cache.
The full Quality graph passes with all cache layers absent.
No node_modules cache is introduced and no Chromium claim is attributed to Bun's package cache.
The measured result is retained with limitations and non-claims.

tasks.title: Route deployment and receipt commands through Turbo and add all cache layers
tasks.goal: Reduce repeated setup and deterministic repository work in Preview, Production, Teardown and Receipt workflows without changing candidate, provider, artifact or receipt authority.
outputs: Trusted workflow Vercel Remote Cache binding for eligible Turbo commands.
Trusted workflow GitHub cache restore/save policy for Bun and, where applicable, Chromium.
Turbo task entrypoints for eligible deterministic deployment and receipt checks/builds.
Receipt and deployment workflow contract coverage proving caches do not replace exact source, stage, plan, provider, hosted or artifact proof.
Plan-only Preview evidence before any authorised mutation workflow proof.
tasks.implementationPrompt: Enable Vercel Remote Cache for every eligible Turbo command in the four workflows and route direct deterministic root/package checks and the provider-free docs build through Turbo task entrypoints where their complete inputs can be hashed. Keep bun install, browser installation, external workflow/artifact reads, Alchemy/provider plans and mutations, provider/hosted readback and receipt promotion live. If an external input cannot be represented in the Turbo hash, keep that checker live and record the reason. Preserve non-cancellable mutation stages, exact candidate admission, equal replan, provider readback, hosted proof, artifact identity and receipt reconciliation. Use the docs deployment runbook and authority model before any hosted mutation.
browserVerification: Run an authorised Preview plan-only workflow and inspect cache restore, candidate identity and no-mutation postcondition.
For any authorised deploy, teardown or production proof, retain the exact workflow receipt, provider readback, hosted browser proof and cache observation.
qualityAudits: Review all four workflow contracts for exact source, stage and mutation locking.
Review that every cached deployment/receipt task includes all external workflow or artifact inputs needed for safe invalidation, or is explicitly kept live.
Review that cache hits cannot promote a stale build or substitute for provider/artifact readback.
Review cache credentials and GitHub permissions remain limited to the existing workflow authority.
Review the deployment runbook's bypass, rollback and escalation instructions.

parentAudit.basis: Review the four workflow diffs, deployment policy fixtures, plan-only or hosted receipts, provider/readback boundaries and documentation impact ledger.
parentAudit.recovery: Revert cache setup only; do not destroy, redeploy or alter provider state as a cache-recovery action.

completionCriteria: All four workflow contracts pass with cache steps and existing authority checks intact.
A Preview plan-only run proves exact candidate admission and no provider mutation.
Any stronger deployment claim has a separately authorised provider and hosted receipt.
Cache failure falls back to the existing deployment setup path.
No cached artifact is promoted as a substitute for the current source/build/provider proof.

tasks.title: Measure, document and close the cache slices
tasks.goal: Accept, revise, remove or mark inconclusive the cache intervention using bounded evidence and current semantic owners.
scope: docs/evidence/releases/ or docs/documentation-audit/ for the dated bounded receipt
outputs: Cold/warm comparison with the four required clocks and hosted run identities.
Accepted cache control records with owner, carrying cost, review trigger, retirement condition and disconfirming evidence.
Updated rollback and cache-bypass instructions.
Explicit terminal outcome: retain, revise, remove or inconclusive.
Explicit no-Changeset rationale.
tasks.implementationPrompt: Re-read the final workflow, Turbo, policy, runbook and SPEC owners together. Update the earliest durable owner rather than copying the result into another summary. Keep dated cache observations separate from current policy and provider state. If the result is inconclusive or unsafe, retain the failed evidence and leave the uncached path as the last-known-good recovery.
browserVerification: Confirm that any retained browser cache claim is backed by a complete browser journey, not a screenshot or install log alone.
qualityAudits: Review the final call graphs against the checked-in workflows and canonical release command.
Review every impact-ledger row for Change required, Preserve or N/A evidence.
Review cache security, task-input correctness, action pinning, rollback, provider authority and non-claims.
Review that no external deployment, publication, registry or public-availability claim was inferred from cache evidence.

parentAudit.basis: Review all task diffs, hosted receipts, cache measurements, architecture and runbook updates, the impact ledger and the final terminal outcome.
parentAudit.recovery: Revert or re-scope the cache slice, retain the uncached workflow as last known good and record the failed or inconclusive evidence outside the default current route.

completionCriteria: Every accepted performance claim has a source revision, workflow run, cache identity, observed postcondition, limitation and non-claim.
The intervention is classified as retain, revise, remove or inconclusive.
All durable owners and lifecycle pointers are aligned.
The parent agent reviewed the final diff and evidence against this SPEC and the repository architecture.
The no-Changeset rationale is recorded.
